questions.question: The CSS Box Model consists of, from outside in:
questions.explanation: Margin is outermost, then border, then padding, then the content box at the center.

questions.question: With box-sizing: border-box, an element's width includes:

options.text: Padding and border (not margin) — width is the total render size

questions.explanation: border-box makes width/height include padding+border, so sizing is predictable. The modern reset sets this globally.

questions.question: display: inline-block differs from inline in that it:

options.text: Respects width/height and vertical padding/margins (stays on same line)
Breaks to a new line always

questions.explanation: inline-block keeps inline flow but accepts box dimensions — great for nav items, buttons in a row.

questions.question: The default display of <div> is:
questions.explanation: div is block-level (full width, stacks vertically); span is inline.

questions.question: A 'block formatting context' (BFC) is created by, among others:

options.text: overflow: hidden, display: flow-root, or float

questions.explanation: BFCs isolate layout (contain floats, prevent margin collapse). display:flow-root creates one cleanly without side effects.

questions.question: Margin collapsing means:

options.text: Adjacent vertical margins of block siblings combine into the larger one

questions.explanation: Vertical margins between siblings (and parent-child in some cases) collapse to the max of the two — a classic layout surprise.

questions.question: To center a block horizontally you use:
questions.explanation: margin: 0 auto centers a fixed-width block; text-align:center only centers inline content.

questions.question: float was originally designed for:

options.text: Wrapping text around images (later abused for full layouts)

questions.explanation: float was for text-wrapping; modern layouts use flex/grid. Clearfix or BFC contains floated children.
